title: Define the canonical public memory API contract
description:
Background

Public docs and runtime behavior currently drift. The public product needs one canonical memory API that is backed by the actual gateway implementation instead of aspirational docs or leaked internal routes.

Dependencies

* Depends on: PIX-226, PIX-227
* Blocks: PIX-230, PIX-231

Scope

Design the versioned public contract for memory features after the gateway boundary is established.

API Areas

* create memory
* list memory
* search memory
* update memory
* delete memory
* optional conversation/session sync if it survives product review

Deliverables

* versioned public route surface
* request/response schema definitions
* error contract aligned with product auth and tenancy behavior
* decision on what remains product-only vs developer-platform-accessible
* contract tests or schema validation coverage

Acceptance Criteria

* public memory API is described from the implemented backend behavior
* no internal Hindsight/MCP route shape leaks into the public contract
* identity and scope fields align with the account/workspace model
* the contract is stable enough to support future SDK work

* Chad

title: Introduce explicit account and workspace memory scoping
description:
Background

The current public edge is still mostly userId-shaped. That is too weak for a real public product because it does not clearly model personal memory versus account/workspace memory or prepare the system for B2B and multi-user scenarios.

Dependencies

* Depends on: PIX-228, PIX-226
* Informs: PIX-229, PIX-231

Scope

Introduce an explicit identity and scope model for memory access in the public product path.

Target Model

* user_id
* account_id or workspace_id
* optional app_id / integration_id
* server-derived memory namespace/scope

Deliverables

* concrete scope model and mapping rules
* backend logic that derives internal memory scope from authenticated product identity
* clear rules for personal vs shared/workspace memory
* tests that prove isolation between users, workspaces, and future integration/app identities

Acceptance Criteria

* memory scope is derived server-side, not trusted from public client input
* two users in different workspaces cannot collide in memory scope
* the model supports both consumer and future B2B/team scenarios
* the scope rules are documented for backend and API usage

Owner

* Chad

Notes

Do not expose internal bank IDs as the public tenant model. The public product should speak in product-native identity concepts, not internal storage primitives.

***Jira:*** [ADHD-102](<https://russianvodka.atlassian.net/browse/ADHD-102>) (migrated from slimshadyme PIX-174)

title: Rewrite public memory docs and onboarding around the real product contract
description:
Background

Current docs still imply a setup model closer to internal infrastructure than product usage. That is support-heavy, confusing, and incompatible with a public rollout.

Dependencies

* Depends on: PIX-225, PIX-226, PIX-229
* Should not begin until the gateway-backed public contract is stable enough to document honestly

Scope

Rewrite public memory documentation and onboarding so they describe the real product boundary rather than the internal service.

Areas To Update

* src/pages/docs/api/index.astro
* src/pages/docs/api/\_openapi.yaml
* src/pages/docs/getting-started.astro
* any memory setup docs that mention internal service URLs, direct host configuration, actor secrets, or bank IDs

Deliverables

* public docs aligned with the canonical gateway-backed contract
* onboarding that reflects either normal app auth or platform API key auth
* removal of direct internal-service setup instructions from public docs
* examples that match the real runtime and auth posture

Acceptance Criteria

* a new user can understand memory setup without learning internal infrastructure details
* docs and runtime behavior match
* no public guide instructs users to expose or configure the internal memory service directly
* examples are validated against the actual implemented API surface

Owner

* Chad

Success Metric

Public onboarding should feel like:

* sign in and memory works

or

* create an app key and call the Pixelated API

It must not feel like:

* choose a bank
* manage actor secrets
* expose port 5003

title: Prepare the developer API and SDK rollout after gateway stabilization
description:
Background

A public developer/API story should be the last step, not the first. The current internal actor-auth model is infrastructure auth, not a public developer experience.

Dependencies

* Should not ship before the gateway, tenancy model, and public contract are already stable

* define how apps map to account/workspace/user scope

* optionally prepare Python SDK support if product demand justifies it

Deliverables

* SDK surface proposal aligned with the real public API contract
* initial rollout plan for external developer access
* clear separation between internal service credentials and public developer credentials

Acceptance Criteria

* no public developer integration depends on internal actor secrets

title: Remove browser-direct internal memory service usage
description:
Background

Several browser/client-side memory paths still imply or directly support communication with the internal memory service boundary. That is incompatible with a public product shape because the browser must never know about internal service URLs, actor auth, Hindsight-compatible routes, or raw infrastructure boundaries.

Why This Is First

This is the first hard boundary cut. Until browser-direct access is removed, the product can continue to drift toward exposing internal infrastructure details.

Dependencies

* Blocks: PIX-228, PIX-226, PIX-230
* Depends on: existing product memory client inventory only

Scope

Remove or neutralize product/client assumptions that point browser code at the internal memory service.

Target Areas

* src/lib/memory/mcp-memory-client.ts
* src/lib/memory/hindsight-client.ts
* any frontend/runtime config that advertises NEXT_PUBLIC_MEMORY_API_URL=[http://localhost:5003](<http://localhost:5003>)
* any browser code path that assumes direct access to the shared service host

Deliverables

* inventory of browser-direct memory-service usage
* implementation changes so browser memory flows only through app/backend routes
* cleanup of public env/config examples that expose internal service URLs
* clear internal note on which modules are allowed to talk to the internal memory service directly

Acceptance Criteria

* no browser bundle path depends on direct access to port 5003
* no public/frontend docs instruct users to configure the internal memory service directly
* all remaining direct memory-service calls are server-side only
* client code compiles and uses backend-owned routes instead of internal service URLs

Owner

* Chad

Notes

Do not solve this by adding more public configuration knobs for the internal service.

***Jira:*** [ADHD-105](<https://russianvodka.atlassian.net/browse/ADHD-105>) (migrated from slimshadyme PIX-177)

title: Public Memory Product Transition Program
description:
### Core Objective

Design and implement the algorithmic reprioritization engine that scores and re-ranks outstanding backlog items based on real-time empirical performance evidence and user session data.

### Technical Design Specs

* **Evidence Collector**:
  * Extract performance gaps, clinical safety alerts, and therapist interaction frequencies from the database.
* **Multi-Criteria Scoring Engine**:
  * Implement a mathematical prioritization model using NumPy/SciPy in Python.
  * Calculate priority scores based on: Severity Weight, Frequency Score, System Performance Gap, and User-Facing Impact.
  * Establish a rank-order sorting routine to output a dynamically prioritized list of open tickets.
* **Priority Sync Bridge**:
  * Map prioritization outputs back to standard Atlassian/Linear priority levels (Highest, High, Medium, Low, Lowest).

### Atlassian & Code Linkages

* **Epic Link**: \[ADHD-9: Steering & Adaptive Development Loop\](file:///home/vivi/pixelated/exports/pix-to-adhd-key-map.json)
* **Primary Source Code**:
  * Prioritization Backend Service: `ai-services/prioritization/engine.py`
  * Math Model Utilities: `ai-services/prioritization/scoring.py`
  * Scoring Tests: `ai-services/tests/test_prioritizer.py`

### Verification & Testing Checklist

- [ ] **Mathematical Verification**: Run python tests verifying that:
  - Higher-impact performance anomalies consistently result in higher ranking shifts.
  - The sorting routine operates with $O(N \\log N)$ complexity, handling 5000 items in `< 100ms`.
  - Randomized perturbations in weights preserve rank ordering constraints.
- [ ] **Consistency Audit**: Verify that calculated priorities match available ticket fields on the target system.

title: Refactor user profile data model and migration plan
description:
### Core Objective

Refactor the user profile data model to consolidate legacy authentication fields, support multi-org/multi-workspace scoping, and implement a safe, rollback-enabled database migration plan.

### Technical Design Specs

* **Data Model Overhaul**:
  * Update user schema to support `workspace_id` and role-based access control (RBAC).
  * Migrate legacy auth fields (auth0/supabase references) into a unified identity provider object.
* **Migration Pipeline**:
  * Write database migration scripts to transition existing user profiles without data loss.
  * Implement a dual-write phase or backward-compatibility layer during transition to prevent service disruption.
  * Setup automated rollback checks in case migration verification fails.

### Verification & Testing Checklist

- [ ] **Unit and Integration Tests**:
  * Run database migration scripts against a mock database populated with legacy user profiles and verify all profiles migrate successfully.
  * Assert that query performance for user profiles remains stable or improves.
- [ ] **Compatibility Check**:
  * Verify that the target SPA and mobile app can authenticate and load profiles correctly under both old and new data model formats.

title: Workstream E: Build evidence-based reprioritization engine
description:
### Core Objective

Design and implement the algorithmic reprioritization engine that scores and re-ranks outstanding backlog items based on real-time empirical performance evidence and user session data.

### Technical Design Specs

* **Evidence Collector**:
  * Extract performance gaps, clinical safety alerts, and therapist interaction frequencies from the database.
* **Multi-Criteria Scoring Engine**:
  * Implement a mathematical prioritization model using NumPy/SciPy in Python.
  * Calculate priority scores based on: Severity Weight, Frequency Score, System Performance Gap, and User-Facing Impact.
  * Establish a rank-order sorting routine to output a dynamically prioritized list of open tickets.
* **Priority Sync Bridge**:
  * Map prioritization outputs back to standard Atlassian/Linear priority levels (Highest, High, Medium, Low, Lowest).

### Atlassian & Code Linkages

* **Epic Link**: \[ADHD-9: Steering & Adaptive Development Loop\](file:///home/vivi/pixelated/exports/pix-to-adhd-key-map.json)
* **Primary Source Code**:
  * Prioritization Backend Service: `ai-services/prioritization/engine.py`
  * Math Model Utilities: `ai-services/prioritization/scoring.py`
  * Scoring Tests: `ai-services/tests/test_prioritizer.py`

### Verification & Testing Checklist

- [ ] **Mathematical Verification**: Run python tests verifying that:
  - Higher-impact performance anomalies consistently result in higher ranking shifts.
  - The sorting routine operates with $O(N \\log N)$ complexity, handling 5000 items in `< 100ms`.
  - Randomized perturbations in weights preserve rank ordering constraints.
- [ ] **Consistency Audit**: Verify that calculated priorities match available ticket fields on the target system.

title: Workstream E: Implement performance-gap-to-backlog conversion rules
description:
### Core Objective

Create the automated rules engine that translates real-time performance gap data (API latencies, high memory consumption, elevated error rates, token waste) into structured, actionable engineering backlog tickets.

### Technical Design Specs

* **Event listener Integration**:
  * Connect a persistent event listener to the central system telemetry collection in MongoDB.
* **Conversion Rule Engine**:
  * Implement heuristics to automatically classify performance drops (e.g. latency spikes > 2s, CPU throttling, elevated 5xx HTTP response rates).
  * Group and deduplicate identical or related events to prevent ticket duplication.
  * Automatically construct a structured backlog issue format mapping performance anomalies to technical tasks.
* **Jira Atlassian Integration**:
  * Integrate with the Atlassian REST SDK to automatically provision backlog tickets under the Jira project.

### Atlassian & Code Linkages

* **Epic Link**: \[ADHD-9: Steering & Adaptive Development Loop\](file:///home/vivi/pixelated/exports/pix-to-adhd-key-map.json)
* **Primary Source Code**:
  * Performance Monitor Listener: `src/services/performance_analyzer.ts`
  * Backlog Converter Rules: `src/services/backlog_converter.ts`
  * Atlassian Connector: `src/lib/atlassian/jira_connector.ts`

### Verification & Testing Checklist

- [ ] **Unit Tests**: Add tests under `tests/backlog-converter.test.ts` verifying that:
  - Telemetry alerts triggers are parsed correctly.
  - Threshold parameters correctly trigger a conversion event.
  - Duplicate events are successfully grouped under a single parent ticket.
- [ ] **Dry Run Validation**: Run the converter rules against mock performance logs and verify that JSON output payloads conform to the Jira ticket schema.

Build the background memory consolidation and summarization engine ("Dreaming") that runs offline to analyze daily interaction logs, synthesize long-term semantic understandings, and execute database garbage collection.

### Technical Design Specs

* **Offline Dream Scheduler**:
  * Implement a cron-based scheduler using BullMQ (backed by local Redis container) to trigger dream consolidation cycles during off-peak hours.
* **Cognitive Summarization Model**:
  * Utilize pre-trained text transformers to extract core therapeutic themes, patient emotional progress markers, and key cognitive behavioral milestones.
  * Save unified, high-level summaries to the patient's long-term memory store in MongoDB.
* **Data Compaction & Garbage Collection**:
  * Prune obsolete, redundant chat logs and temporary caches to keep database storage footprint optimized.
  * Ensure correct primary key references are maintained across compacted collections.

### Atlassian & Code Linkages

* **Epic Link**: \[ADHD-21: Cognitive Reflection and Offline Processing\](file:///home/vivi/pixelated/exports/pix-to-adhd-key-map.json)
* **Primary Source Code**:
  * Dream Scheduler Service: `src/services/dream_scheduler.ts`
  * ML Summarization Task: `ai-services/dream/consolidation.py`
  * Worker Handler: `src/workers/dream_worker.ts`

### Verification & Testing Checklist

- [ ] **Integration Tests**: Write an integration suite verifying that a completed dream consolidation cycle successfully:
  - Produces a coherent long-term memory document.
  - Deletes raw session caches as configured.
  - Maintains strict referential integrity.
- [ ] **Memory Indexing Performance**: Audit read/write query latency before and after running a dream cycle, ensuring indexing speeds are improved by at least 15%.
- [ ] **Failure Recovery**: Interrupt a dream worker mid-processing and confirm that the system handles job retries via Redis seamlessly without duplicating summaries.

title: Sprint 2: Gating & Ingestion (May 26 – June 8)
description:
### Core Objective

Implement the real-time clinical safety and data ingestion gating layer to screen all conversational inputs, evaluate safety levels, detect high emotional arousal, and route messages dynamically.

### Technical Design Specs

* **Ingestion Pipeline**:
  * Build an async ingestion pipeline using Fast API in `ai-services` that intermediates between the React UI layer and the core memory storage adapter.
  * Integrate an LLM-based safety classifier that screens patient inputs against defined diagnostic criteria.
* **React UI Gating Integration**:
  * Design React components displaying real-time screening states (Ingesting, Gating, Safety Verified, Routed) using micro-animations.
  * Provide immediate feedback to the therapist if critical safety flags (e.g. self-harm, severe crisis) are detected.
* **Safety Routing Engine**:
  * Route standard messages to standard memory collections and flag high-arousal messages for immediate professional escalation.

### Verification & Testing Checklist

- [ ] **Performance Profiling**: Run load testing simulating 100 concurrent chat session ingestions and verify average response time remains `< 200ms`.

* Map evaluation failures to likely upstream causes
* Turn measured quality gaps into concrete dataset interventions
* Feed new priorities back into acquisition, curation, and review work
* Make the pipeline improve through evidence rather than intuition alone

* Instrument stage throughput and readiness state
* Surface validation failures and regressions
* Make pipeline health visible enough to support operational decisions
* Reduce hidden failure accumulation across the pipeline

Define the validation gates and failure criteria that determine whether a dataset is training-ready. This issue owns the readiness definition, validation failure criteria, and the gate-checking infrastructure that downstream packaging and observability depend on.

title: 2.0 Create MultilingualSafetyChecker
description:
Create `ai/training/multilingual_safety_checker.py` extending `ClinicalSafetyChecker`:

* Crisis patterns for Spanish, French, Portuguese, German (min 6 per language: suicide, self-harm, want to die, no reason to live, cutting, medication overdose)
* Negation patterns per language; asymmetric negation-window (100 chars before, 30 chars after)
* `VERSION = "1.0.0"`, `supported_languages = ["en", "es", "fr", "pt", "de"]`
* Unknown language → apply all pattern sets, return `True` on any match

title: [GAP-1] Implement vector search with embeddings
description:
Background

The shared memory service is already operational and durable, but it is internal infrastructure. The public product needs a backend-owned gateway layer that terminates product auth, translates identity and scope, and calls the internal memory service with server-held credentials.

Dependencies

* Depends on: PIX-225
* Blocks: PIX-226, PIX-229, PIX-230, PIX-231

Scope

Design and implement a product memory gateway inside the app/backend surface.

Responsibilities

* accept normal user/session auth and future product API auth
* translate product identity into internal memory scope
* call the shared memory service using server-held actor credentials
* normalize errors and response shapes
* centralize policy, quota, and tenancy checks
* keep internal service details fully hidden from public consumers

Deliverables

* dedicated gateway module/service abstraction in the app/backend
* internal client wrapper for the shared memory service
* auth and scope translation model
* shared error and response mapping contract
* tests for success, auth failure, scope mismatch, and downstream service failure

Acceptance Criteria

* app/backend memory operations go through one gateway abstraction
* no route/controller duplicates raw shared-service request logic
* gateway uses server-held credentials only
* failures from the internal memory service are translated into product-safe responses
* the gateway can serve as the sole public boundary for memory features

Owner

* Chad

Suggested File Areas

* src/pages/api/memory/\*
* app/backend auth layer
* product server utilities and internal API clients
* shared runtime config for service-to-service auth

Execution Notes (2026-04-02)

* 55053b9a8 - add shared-service backup and monitoring automation

title: Implement hook system for memory operations
description:
## Pattern

Django Signals + FastAPI Events hybrid

## Hooks to Implement

* `pre_store`: Before memory storage (validation, transformation)
* `post_store`: After storage (indexing, notifications)
* `pre_retrieve`: Before retrieval (auth, filtering)
* `post_retrieve`: After retrieval (analytics, caching)
* `pre_update`: Before update (conflict detection)
* `post_update`: After update (projections, sync)
* `pre_delete`: Before deletion (soft delete, backup)
* `post_delete`: After deletion (cleanup, audit)

## Implementation

1. Create `HookManager` with `register()`, `trigger()`, `unregister()`
2. Hook decorators for Python functions
3. Priority ordering (higher priority executes first)
4. Async hook support with `asyncio.gather()`
5. Error handling with continue-on-error option

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `HookManager` with full lifecycle
- [ ] All 8 hook points implemented
- [ ] Priority ordering works correctly
- [ ] Async hooks supported
- [ ] Error handling doesn't break main flow
- [ ] Hook execution logged for audit
- [ ] Tests for all hook scenarios

description:
## Master plan for AutoReview AI workflow improvements.

After processing \~50 PRs across 6 runs on `daggerstuff/pixelated`:

* **27 merged** successfully
* **19 blocked** by merge conflicts
* **17+ LLM fixes** generated and applied
* **1 draft** skipped

### Key Findings from Real-World Testing

* **80% of failures** are merge conflicts, not fix failures → auto-rebase is P0
* **Most PRs need no fixing** → fast-path gives 3x throughput
* **AI comments on AI code** → circular validation, need to prioritize human comments
* **Token economy is inverted** → spending most tokens on least valuable PRs
* **Real value is triage, not fixing** → autonomous PR management > autonomous PR fixing

title: Remove browser-direct internal memory service usage
description:
Background

Several browser/client-side memory paths still imply or directly support communication with the internal memory service boundary. That is incompatible with a public product shape because the browser must never know about internal service URLs, actor auth, Hindsight-compatible routes, or raw infrastructure boundaries.

Why This Is First

This is the first hard boundary cut. Until browser-direct access is removed, the product can continue to drift toward exposing internal infrastructure details.

Dependencies

* Blocks: PIX-228, PIX-226, PIX-230
* Depends on: existing product memory client inventory only

Scope

Remove or neutralize product/client assumptions that point browser code at the internal memory service.

Target Areas

* src/lib/memory/mcp-memory-client.ts
* src/lib/memory/hindsight-client.ts
* any frontend/runtime config that advertises NEXT_PUBLIC_MEMORY_API_URL=[http://localhost:5003](<http://localhost:5003>)
* any browser code path that assumes direct access to the shared service host

Deliverables

* inventory of browser-direct memory-service usage
* implementation changes so browser memory flows only through app/backend routes
* cleanup of public env/config examples that expose internal service URLs
* clear internal note on which modules are allowed to talk to the internal memory service directly

Acceptance Criteria

* no browser bundle path depends on direct access to port 5003
* no public/frontend docs instruct users to configure the internal memory service directly
* all remaining direct memory-service calls are server-side only
* client code compiles and uses backend-owned routes instead of internal service URLs

Owner

* Chad

Notes

Do not solve this by adding more public configuration knobs for the internal service.

**Jira:** [ADHD-105](<https://russianvodka.atlassian.net/browse/ADHD-105>) (migrated from slimshadyme PIX-177)

title: Introduce explicit account and workspace memory scoping
description:

The current public edge is still mostly userId-shaped. That is too weak for a real public product because it does not clearly model personal memory versus account/workspace memory or prepare the system for B2B and multi-user scenarios.

* Informs: PIX-229, PIX-231

Scope

Target Model

* user_id
* account_id or workspace_id
* optional app_id / integration_id
* server-derived memory namespace/scope

Deliverables

* concrete scope model and mapping rules
* backend logic that derives internal memory scope from authenticated product identity
* clear rules for personal vs shared/workspace memory
* tests that prove isolation between users, workspaces, and future integration/app identities

* memory scope is derived server-side, not trusted from public client input

* the model supports both consumer and future B2B/team scenarios

title: Workstream D: Define training-ready packaging and automation plan
description:
# Workstream D: Define training-ready packaging and automation plan

## Objective

Define how curated stage-sliced datasets are packaged into promotion-ready artifacts. Integrates with training readiness gates ([PIX-506](https://linear.app/pixelated/issue/PIX-506/workstream-d-define-training-readiness-validation-gates)) to produce validated, self-describing dataset packages.

## Package Model

Each package is a self-contained bundle containing:

* `manifest.json`: Package metadata and validation status
* `data.jsonl`: Serialized records in canonical format
* `metrics.json`: Quality metrics snapshot
* `readiness_report.json`: [PIX-506](https://linear.app/pixelated/issue/PIX-506/workstream-d-define-training-readiness-validation-gates) validation output
* `promotion_token.json`: Promotion eligibility proof (if can_promote=True)

## Verified Files

* `ai/core/pipelines/packaging.py` (308 lines) — DatasetPackager, PackageBundle, PackageStatus
* `ai/core/pipelines/test_packaging.py` (269 lines) — 12 passing tests
* `ai/core/pipelines/training_ready/` — Generated training-ready data directory

## Audit Note (2026-05-23)

This issue was marked Done but had no `startedAt` date, no verified files listed, and its code depended on `training_readiness_gates.py` which had a SyntaxError (fixed in [PIX-506](https://linear.app/pixelated/issue/PIX-506/workstream-d-define-training-readiness-validation-gates) audit). After the [PIX-506](https://linear.app/pixelated/issue/PIX-506/workstream-d-define-training-readiness-validation-gates) fix, packaging module imports and tests pass (12/12). The original description was a vague placeholder; replaced with accurate scope.

title: CI Federation & Release Readiness
description:
### Core Objective

Coordinate the CI federation initiative so release readiness is standardized, Azure remains the sole deploy authority, duplicate job ownership is resolved, and provider-specific validation lanes are intentionally designed instead of overlapping by accident.

Problem statement

The CI landscape spans multiple providers and accumulated overlap. This epic groups the work required to define lane ownership, reduce duplicate execution, and make release gates explicit.

In scope

* define the readiness model and gate contract
* map ownership and remove duplicate non-owner jobs
* standardize command contracts across CI providers
* keep MR, security, AI validation, and deploy lanes intentionally separated by purpose
* add dashboarding and failure-to-ticket workflows where operationally useful

Exit criteria

* one deploy authority is enforced
* readiness signal and pass criteria are defined and implemented
* cross-provider command usage is standardized
* owners, reviews, escalation paths, and dashboard expectations are documented

| Expertise | ≥75% | ≥50% | 100% | ≥75% | 50% |

## Audit Note (2026-05-23)

**Code fix applied:** `stage_slicer_enhanced.py` had a `SyntaxError: keyword argument repeated: safety_floor` in all four `StageConfig` constructors. title: Build the product memory gateway over the shared service
description:
Background

The shared memory service is already operational and durable, but it is internal infrastructure. The public product needs a backend-owned gateway layer that terminates product auth, translates identity and scope, and calls the internal memory service with server-held credentials.

Dependencies

* Depends on: PIX-225
* Blocks: PIX-226, PIX-229, PIX-230, PIX-231

Scope

Design and implement a product memory gateway inside the app/backend surface.

Responsibilities

* accept normal user/session auth and future product API auth
* translate product identity into internal memory scope
* call the shared memory service using server-held actor credentials
* normalize errors and response shapes
* centralize policy, quota, and tenancy checks
* keep internal service details fully hidden from public consumers

Deliverables

* dedicated gateway module/service abstraction in the app/backend
* internal client wrapper for the shared memory service
* auth and scope translation model
* shared error and response mapping contract
* tests for success, auth failure, scope mismatch, and downstream service failure

Acceptance Criteria

* app/backend memory operations go through one gateway abstraction
* no route/controller duplicates raw shared-service request logic
* gateway uses server-held credentials only
* failures from the internal memory service are translated into product-safe responses
* the gateway can serve as the sole public boundary for memory features

Owner

* Chad

Suggested File Areas

* src/pages/api/memory/\*
* app/backend auth layer
* product server utilities and internal API clients
* shared runtime config for service-to-service auth

Execution Notes (2026-04-02)

Progress shipped on staging for shared-service operational hardening:

* 55053b9a8 - add shared-service backup and monitoring automation
  * added backup/restore scripts for SQLite memory DB
  * added health + disk monitor script
  * added systemd service/timer templates for backup and monitor runs
* e0bc9920b - backup pruning behavior fix
  * made retention prune non-fatal with explicit warning logging

Files delivered:

* scripts/memory/backup-shared-memory-db.sh

* scripts/memory/install-systemd-memory-ops.sh

title: Public Memory Product Transition Program
description:
### Core Objective

Design and implement the algorithmic reprioritization engine that scores and re-ranks outstanding backlog items based on real-time empirical performance evidence and user session data.

### Technical Design Specs

* **Evidence Collector**:
  * Extract performance gaps, clinical safety alerts, and therapist interaction frequencies from the database.
* **Multi-Criteria Scoring Engine**:
  * Implement a mathematical prioritization model using NumPy/SciPy in Python.
  * Calculate priority scores based on: Severity Weight, Frequency Score, System Performance Gap, and User-Facing Impact.
  * Establish a rank-order sorting routine to output a dynamically prioritized list of open tickets.
* **Priority Sync Bridge**:
  * Map prioritization outputs back to standard Atlassian/Linear priority levels (Highest, High, Medium, Low, Lowest).

### Atlassian & Code Linkages

* **Epic Link**: \[ADHD-9: Steering & Adaptive Development Loop\](file:///home/vivi/pixelated/exports/pix-to-adhd-key-map.json)
* **Primary Source Code**:
  * Prioritization Backend Service: `ai-services/prioritization/engine.py`
  * Math Model Utilities: `ai-services/prioritization/scoring.py`
  * Scoring Tests: `ai-services/tests/test_prioritizer.py`

### Verification & Testing Checklist

- [ ] **Mathematical Verification**: Run python tests verifying that:
  - Higher-impact performance anomalies consistently result in higher ranking shifts.
  - The sorting routine operates with $O(N \\log N)$ complexity, handling 5000 items in `< 100ms`.
  - Randomized perturbations in weights preserve rank ordering constraints.
- [ ] **Consistency Audit**: Verify that calculated priorities match available ticket fields on the target system.

title: Refactor user profile data model and migration plan
description:
### Core Objective

Refactor the user profile data model to consolidate legacy authentication fields, support multi-org/multi-workspace scoping, and implement a safe, rollback-enabled database migration plan.

### Technical Design Specs

* **Data Model Overhaul**:
  * Update user schema to support `workspace_id` and role-based access control (RBAC).
  * Migrate legacy auth fields (auth0/supabase references) into a unified identity provider object.
* **Migration Pipeline**:
  * Write database migration scripts to transition existing user profiles without data loss.
  * Implement a dual-write phase or backward-compatibility layer during transition to prevent service disruption.
  * Setup automated rollback checks in case migration verification fails.

### Verification & Testing Checklist

- [ ] **Unit and Integration Tests**:
  * Run database migration scripts against a mock database populated with legacy user profiles and verify all profiles migrate successfully.
  * Assert that query performance for user profiles remains stable or improves.
- [ ] **Compatibility Check**:
  * Verify that the target SPA and mobile app can authenticate and load profiles correctly under both old and new data model formats.

description:
# Workstream A: Consolidate acquisition report and next backlog

## Objective

Consolidate acquisition findings and reporting into a decision-ready backlog. Convert pilot evidence and source-quality data into the next canonical acquisition backlog, ensuring coverage gaps and next-source priorities are visible and actionable.

## Operational responsibility

* Consolidate acquisition reporting across pilots
